title: Fleet Controls: Guardrails, Live Throughput Heatmap, and Immutable Change Audit
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Operators using Redwood Dedicated need clearer, low-friction controls to set throughput guarantees and autoscale policies for fleets and a single place to inspect both live throughput and the complete immutable history of control changes. Existing console panels surface throughput and scaling rules in scattered places; customers have asked for: 1) a guardrail-first UX that prevents accidental overprovisioning, 2) a live heatmap to correlate load to scaling decisions, and 3) a tamper-proof audit trail for compliance and troubleshooting.

Goal: Ship a Fleet Controls page that unifies scaling guardrails (min/max, burst caps, SLO-backed targets), a real-time throughput heatmap over selectable windows, and an immutable change audit view with links to rollout events, PRs, and operator notes. The experience should enable on-call and platform teams to: set safe defaults, preview autoscale policy simulations, and quickly root-cause policy-driven capacity changes.

Out of scope: full RBAC rework (handled by ENG-19512), private deployment agent-side enforcement, and long-term data retention (>13 months).
acceptance_criteria: Console has a Fleet Controls tab for Dedicated fleets accessible from fleet list
Guardrail editor supports min_concurrency, max_capacity_pct, burst_window_ms, and SLO-target fields with validation and suggested defaults
Live throughput heatmap displays per-shard and aggregate QPS, P50/P95 latency, and autoscale events over a selectable 1h/6h/24h window
Audit view is append-only, shows user, timestamp, before/after diff, and links to associated rollout/PR or incident
Operators can run a policy simulation for past 24h traffic and see projected capacity and cost delta
Telemetry events emitted for guardrail changes, simulations, and audit exports
End-to-end e2e test covering guardrail create/update, heatmap load, and audit pagination exists
implementation_notes: Frontend: new FleetControls React route + components for GuardrailEditor, HeatmapPanel, and AuditTable. Use existing charting library and shared time-range selector.

Backend: expose /fleets/{id}/guardrails endpoints (GET/PUT), /fleets/{id}/throughput for heatmap (paginated), and /fleets/{id}/audit (append-only). Backfill last 30 days for heatmap via existing metrics store.
Policy simulation: reuse autoscaler simulator service from ENG-18291 with a small wrapper that accepts guardrail deltas and historical metric slice.
Data model: audit entries stored with cryptographic signature (server-side) and immutable flag to support compliance checks. Coordinate with security for key rotation plan.
Performance: heatmap queries must return initial payload < 350ms for 24h requests in production-scale fleets; caching layer to be evaluated with infra team.
testing_plan: Unit tests for guardrail validation rules and SLO-target parsing
Integration tests for metrics ingestion -> heatmap aggregation -> UI rendering (mocked metrics store)
Load test for heatmap endpoint with synthetic 10k shards to validate query path latency
Security review for audit immutability claim (check key handling)
rollout_plan: Canary: enable Fleet Controls feature flag for 5 internal fleets
Beta: opt-in for customers with dedicated capacity who consent to temporary metric backfill
Full rollout: enable by default after 2 weeks of beta with monitoring for error budget and UI performance
Migration: no DB migration required; audit table will be created as a new append-only collection and populated by service on first change
notes: Design decision: prefer guardrail presets (cost-saver, latency-first, throughput-first) to reduce operator cognitive load. Priya recommended three presets during review on 2026-02-22.

Trade-off: storing full before/after policy blobs in the audit increases storage but simplifies forensics. Diego suggested keeping diffs only; we chose full blobs for first release for easier rollbacks.
Open question: whether to allow rollback from audit UI or require operator to create an explicit guardrail change. Tentatively require explicit change for audit integrity (agreed 2026-03-03).
Cost note: Simulation runs are CPU-bound; we will throttle simulation concurrency to 4 per-org to avoid spikes (see ENG-19004).
Accessibility: components flagged for a11y review during Cycle 2026-W11
